elements.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 28.1: "This Agreement is governed exclusively by New York law." — Singapore law replaced with New York law.

elements.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
elements.evidence: Retained § 28.2 grants exclusive jurisdiction to "[t]he state and federal courts located in New York County, New York" with an irrevocable submission and venue/forum non conveniens waiver; the only carve-out is "temporary injunctive relief in another court," a customary carve-out that does not defeat the exclusive merits forum. The conflicting Singapore forum words in § 28.1 were deleted, so no contradictory retained sentence remains.

elements.element: The governing law is Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 28.1 selects New York law, not Delaware, California, or England and Wales. Not met at the fallback level (the preferred level is satisfied instead).

elements.element: The dispute forum is the corresponding Delaware or California courts, or the courts of London for England and Wales law.
elements.evidence: Forum is New York County state and federal courts, not Delaware/California courts or the courts of London. Not met at the fallback level (the preferred level is satisfied instead).

reasons: The preferred checklist is complete: § 28.1 now designates New York law and retained § 28.2 supplies exclusive New York County merits jurisdiction with only a temporary-injunctive-relief carve-out.

The edit touched only the jurisdiction words and the conflicting Singapore forum phrase; § 28.2, the injunctive carve-out, and all surrounding language are untouched. Deleting the Singapore forum words was necessary to cure the direct conflict with § 28.2's exclusive New York forum, so it is within the checklist rather than a gratuitous deletion.
No extras were added — no survival tail, no arbitration mechanic, no additional procedures or boilerplate.

Intent is preserved: no dangling cross-reference or undefined term results; 'confidential information' and 'intellectual property' in § 28.2 remain intact, and the two sections are now internally consistent rather than contradictory.
The fallback level is not met, but that is immaterial because position-completeness is satisfied at the preferred level.
